data.author: BTCxanter
data.body: I examined all of AoiNakamoto’s stories on Wattpad. The MD5 hash does not match in instances where Aoi has modified the text—for example, by adding a note like "Solved in 90 minutes" to a story that had already been published. This is an important observation.

data.author: BTCxanter
data.body:
Who solved this part? I only found the source text.

MD5: 7759227d7406d8230d7e3a8f7b9846d7

first seven digits: 7759227



text = "I thought I would write a bit about the format for block 77, giving a simple example for that.\\n\\nAs is already clear from the reference to block 29, people are supposed to keep the whole long text and change only a couple of letters in their capitalization.\\n\\nFor example, if the letter \\"n\\" at the end of the last paragraph was part of the solution, you would be expected to change it to \\"N\\" and write \\"capitalizatioN\\".\\n\\nFor what it's worth, that \\"n\\" is not part of the solution, which is obvious to anyone able to recognize the signs.\\n\\nI expected otherwise, but actually not many people do recognize the signs in Satoshi's Bitcointalk post outing himself. Even after I explained the method used and the result in detail.\\n\\nOn the other hand, if you were able to recognize the signs and thought that the \\"I\\" at the beginning of the previous paragraph was one of them, you would be expected to change that \\"I\\" as well to a \\"i\\".\\n\\nWhen you do that, you would end up changing \\"I\\" to \\"i\\" and \\"himself\\" to \\"himselF\\".\\n\\nWhich would be the solution, once you do that for all the paragraphs where you recognize the signs. And keep the rest completely unchanged.\\n\\nI think this easy example should be enough to completely clear up the remaining problems with finding the correct format for both stages of block 77. Should not take too long until someone sees the light now. At least for the first stage...\\n\\nAnd it should be someone mining with the mind. While it may be possible to write a script for this, it should be faster to solve by the thinking only method."

Can anyone who has solved this help? The first three digits of the MD5 hash are 3c6.

data.author: BTCxanter
data.body: The only anomaly in the "Second" chapter is line 78. Its MD5 hash 8b71bade9685d3388452bc4755b06a0d doesn't match if the word is "What?". That is likely the puzzle. We need to find the sentence that unlocks this MD5 hash. Let's go, solvers!
